question: Two of the 37 members first seated 1932–1962 still have no row, Smith (B. M.) and Lowry. The Evening Star on loc.gov has been read over the whole term for both and printed no street for either; the Star's B. M. Smith of Arlington is a real-estate dealer at 443 Columbia Pike, an office. Dugan, Ames, DeLashmutt and McShea now have a census row each, read off the sheet, but the matches are weak: Dugan is a 23-year-old artist in 1940 who would be 30 when seated, Ames's street label is an abbreviation after W. Lee that could not be resolved and his house number reads 688 where the index gives 436, DeLashmutt's line carries no house number, and McShea is matched on the initial and surname. The 1880, 1900 and 1910 sheets for the pre-1932 members carry no street in Alexandria County's rural districts, so none were read further.
settles: For Smith the 1930 and 1940 censuses under variant spellings and a Clarendon city directory; for Lowry the 1960 census or a city directory, since the Star prints no street; for Ames a stronger read of the 1940 label and house number; a row per finding
